key_insight: Microbial community stability depends on self-limitation, metabolic efficiency and plasticity, while hierarchical trophic organization can counteract destabilizing cross-feeding loops.
engineering_relevance: The framework could inform the design of resilient microbial consortia for bioprocessing, rather than solid-mechanics applications.
method: Develop a generalized model of resource competition and cross-feeding.
Analyze stability across ensembles with varied community sizes, structures and nonlinear dynamics.
Identify metabolic, dynamical and organizational drivers of stability.
evidence_signal: Model-ensemble analysis links stability to community size and metabolic dynamics; the abstract reports no experimental validation or quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Stability conclusions need validation against measured microbial dynamics before guiding engineered community design.
paper_title: Generalized modeling reveals stabilizing mechanisms in cross-feeding microbial communities
